title: Patacara
hookLine: she loses husband, children and parents in one day and runs wild; the Buddha says, sister, recover your mind

lines: A WALK HOME, AND A STORM.
cards: This week is hard stories, and today's is the hardest to hear, so breathe as you listen. Some overwhelm isn't one blow but many, landing before you've gotten up from the last. The mind just can't hold any more.
Patacara was the daughter of a wealthy family in Savatthi. She fell in love with a servant in her parents' house and ran away with him, and they lived poor, far from her family.
Pregnant with their second child, she set out with her husband and little son to walk home to her parents. And a storm came.

teach.h: A STORM, A SNAKE, A RIVER.
teach.b: The story comes from the commentaries; i'll tell it plainly and briefly. In the storm, she gives birth by the road. Her husband goes to find branches for shelter, a snake bites him, and he dies.

In the morning, with a newborn and a toddler, she reaches a river swollen with rain. She carries the baby across first, lays him on the far bank, and turns back for her older son. A hawk swoops toward the baby.
She waves and shouts to scare it off, and her little boy, on the other bank, thinks she's calling him, steps into the river, and is swept away. The hawk takes the baby.
At Savatthi a traveler tells her that in the night's storm her parents' house fell, killing her mother, father and brother. She can see the smoke of their cremation. Her mind breaks.

teach.h: SHE RUNS WILD THROUGH THE CITY.
teach.b: She runs through the streets, her clothes falling away, and people throw dirt at her and chase her off. She runs into the grove where the Buddha is teaching. People try to stop her.
When she's near, he says: sister, recover your mind. Sister. Not madwoman.
Not sinner. She comes back to herself. Someone throws her a cloak.
She sits at his feet and tells him everything. He listens. He doesn't tell her it didn't happen.
He tells her that across the long round of lives, the tears shed for loved ones are more than the water in the oceans. She isn't alone in it.

teach.h: A TEACHER OF WOMEN WHO LOST.
teach.b: Patacara became a nun, and in time a teacher of other women.
Her verses survive in the Therigatha, beside verses from women who came to her grieving.

how: Buddhists remember Patacara as a great nun and teacher of women, honored for her mastery of the monastic discipline, and her verses and those of her students are preserved in the Therigatha.

o: a woman who lost everyone, then taught grieving women
a merchant's wife who sailed to trade across the sea
a queen who gave the Buddha a grove to teach in

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: thrown to her as she came to herself
less than the tears shed for loved ones

s: the Buddha told Patacara her losses weren't real
he told her the tears shed for loved ones are more than the oceans. she wasn't alone.
people tried to keep her away, and he said let her come
Patacara became a teacher of other women
the Therigatha keeps verses from women who came to her grieving.

games.q: a woman runs into the grove, wild with grief, clothes falling away. people try to drive her off. you're the teacher. what do you do?
o: let her come, and speak to her gently.
games.why: he says let her come, and says: sister, recover your mind. she comes back to herself, and someone gives her a cloak.

practice: Put one hand on your chest; breathe in for four, hold a moment, and breathe out for six, the out-breath always longer. If you like, let a word ride on it, the way Patacara heard one word: sister.
Learned while calm, the way back is there when you're overwhelmed.

wordCard.voice: Patacara. The woman who lost everyone in a day, heard the words, sister, recover your mind, and became a teacher of women.

orig.note: Pali: sister. What the Buddha called Patacara as she came toward him.

carryVoice: Your line: recover your mind. The way back can start with one word. That's seventy-six.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 15.3 (tears more than the four oceans)
